newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Still no IMF agreement on Ivory Coast loan - source.
newsitem.headline: Still no IMF agreement on Ivory Coast loan - source.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team ended a meeting with the Ivory Coast government last week without full agreement on the terms of an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (EAF), a donor source said on Monday.

Agreement was reached on liberalising the cocoa and coffee sectors, but there were "a couple of things to resolve," the source said. That means a draft agreement was highly unlikely to be ready for the next IMF board meeting in September.
The two sides would continue to exchange information over the next week, the source said, but he declined to reveal what the sticking points were.
The IMF team has now left Abidjan.

Securing an IMF structural adjustment agreement is crucial if Ivory Coast is to get further rescheduling of its official debt owed to governments in the Paris Club and get a wider debt write-off under the donor community's Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative.
The source also noted an IMF deal was necessary to provide the "up-front" money to back a debt reduction deal with commercial banks, signed after years of tough negotiations in May.
